prompt: Which statement about leverage is correct?

options.text: Leverage increases the expected profit of the same trades.
Leverage makes gains and losses bigger by the same factor. It does not change the expected result of the bet.
Leverage removes the risk of a bad trade once the margin is paid.
Leverage only affects losses, not gains.

explanations.a: Leverage scales the rupee gains and losses. It does not raise the average result of the same bets.
explanations.c: The full contract value is still exposed to price moves. The margin does not remove that risk.
explanations.d: Leverage works in both directions. Gains grow by the same factor as losses.

prompt: When do gains and losses on a futures position move in your account?

options.text: Only at expiry, on the last day of the contract.
Only when you close the position yourself.
As prices move, day by day, not only at expiry.
Only when the exchange pays out the profit in one sum.

explanations.a: This is the wrong idea. Daily settlement moves money as prices change, before expiry.
explanations.b: Closing the position does not decide when money moves. Daily settlement has already moved it.
explanations.d: Money does not wait for one payout at the end. It moves as prices change.

prompt: A trader puts Rs 1,00,000 in margin on a futures position. Which statement about the most the trader can lose is correct?

options.text: The most I can lose is the margin deposited.
Losses can be larger than the margin deposited, so the deposit is not a limit on loss.
The loss can never be more than the profit I hoped to make.
Losses only count at expiry, so the deposit is safe until then.

explanations.a: The margin is not a cap. Prices can move against the position by more than the deposit.
explanations.c: A hoped-for profit does not limit a loss. The loss follows the price move.
explanations.d: Daily settlement moves losses in and out as prices change. They are not held until expiry.

prompt: Hypothetical. Contract value Rs 10,00,000 and margin Rs 1,00,000. The price moves 2% against the position. What is the rupee loss on the contract?
Hypothetical. Same case as the previous question. The loss is what percent of the margin deposited? Give one decimal place.
Hypothetical. Your cash in the account is Rs 50,000. A futures position moves Rs 60,000 against you in one day. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The loss is smaller than the cash, so nothing more can happen.
The loss is bigger than your cash, and you may have to pay more money into the account.
The loss is capped at Rs 50,000, the cash you hold.
Nothing happens until expiry, so the account is fine today.

explanations.a: Rs 60,000 is larger than Rs 50,000. The loss is bigger than the cash, not smaller.
explanations.c: The cash in the account is not a cap on the loss. The move can be larger than the cash held.
explanations.d: Losses move through the account as prices change, not only at expiry.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "Futures are a cheaper way to hold the same stock." Which part is wrong?

options.text: The word futures: a futures contract is an agreement for a set price on a set date.
The word cheaper: the small deposit is not a lower cost or a lower risk.
The word stock: a stock and a futures contract are the same kind of asset.
Nothing. The statement is correct.

explanations.a: A futures contract is an agreement for a set price on a set date. This word is correct.
explanations.c: A share is ownership of part of a company. A futures contract is an agreement with an expiry date. They are not the same kind of asset.
explanations.d: The statement is wrong. A small deposit does not lower the risk, and the contract ends on a set date.
